summary.headline: HOEC Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose to INR117.5 crore from negative INR194 crore, but PBT before exceptionals fell to INR12.5 crore on B-80 water cut and HPCL crude resale losses.
summary.overview: Standalone net revenue after profit petroleum and revenue share was INR107.6 crore, versus a prior quarter hit by the INR259 crore HPCL sale reversal. Kharsang output rose from about 12,300 to 17,400 BOE, and crude realisation improved to about $95.5/bbl from $70.8. Profitability weakened: standalone PBT before exceptionals was INR12.5 crore (versus INR30.4 crore) and consolidated PBT was INR6.5 crore (versus INR9.0 crore), partly due to crude inventory accounting. B-80 production remained constrained by rising water cut, with workovers now planned after monsoon and funding for the B-80 programme dependent on debt the company is still raising.

segments.name: B-80 (offshore, Bombay)
segments.commentary: Production hit by higher water cut in one producing well; compressor trains reconfigured to series and in test mode, with output partial. Crude liquidation from HPCL tanks began but slower than expected; about 15% sold so far, with losses estimated at INR4-6 crore and further loss guided at 7-10% of inventory.

segments.name: Kharsang (Assam)
segments.commentary: Production rose from about 12,300 to 17,400 BOE QoQ after nine-well programme and workovers on 23 shut-in wells (5-6 done). Second phase of nine wells pending rig award and tubulars in 1-2 months. Virgin gas found in two wells with no pipeline; route survey tender closes next day, 24 km pipeline targeted in 14-18 months.

segments.name: Dirok (Assam, operator, ~27% interest)
segments.commentary: Reservoir capable of higher output, but only 50-70% of well capability is produced due to evacuation constraints. DNPL line capacity reduced to about 1-1.5 MMSCMD from 2.5 MMSCMD design; hot-tap tie-ins by AGCL targeted for December.

segments.name: PY-1 (East Coast)
segments.commentary: Three wells suffered serious production loss. Rig-less intervention contracted and self-funded for near-term output. Two new wells (est. 15-20 MMSCFD) to be drilled only after take-or-pay gas agreement with GAIL or IOCL; previously planned for Q4 next year.

segments.name: Cambay (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Palej debottlenecking and Balol belt technology in trial; management expects 20-30% output increase, with 5-6% already achieved last quarter. Sucker rod pumps ordered; new exploration block in final approval stage.

segments.name: B-15 (new block)
segments.commentary: Holds 16 MMBOE per management, subject to reappraisal. FDP under preparation with three to four concepts, one involving connection to ONGC platform. Drilling planned for FY28.

guidance_outlook: Dirok evacuation: hot-tap tie-ins and DNPL capacity restoration targeted by end-December; DNPL capacity expected to return to about 2.5 MMSCMD at 90 bar, with locked-in volumes of 0.5-0.7 MMSCMD gross for HOEC.

B-80 workovers of two wells (D1, D2) to be mobilised after rig award, targeted by October; two workovers on production by Nov-Dec 2026, three new wells on production by June 2027, with 500-800 bbl per well expected.
B-80 stored crude in HPCL tanks: management expects inventory cleared by end-October or early November; first small-tanker sale of 120,000-130,000 bbl planned for October.
Management expects cash flows to fund B-15 growth by November-December 2027; B-80 programme to be debt-funded, with the company in process of raising debt.
Capex: management said the increased capex budget is a contingency facility to be drawn as needed, given rig tightness.
capex_capacity: B-80: single campaign of two workovers (10-20 days each) and three new wells (30-40 days each), then jacket and production deck installation, with production start around end-March/early April 2027 per plan, subject to delays.
Dirok: DNPL line degraded; sections being replaced and tied back via hot taps by AGCL; NRL 150-200 m bypass pipeline inside refinery is a parallel item.
Kharsang: second phase of nine wells pending rig award; tubulars ordered; pipeline to Bordumsa (Oil India line) 24 km, 14-18 months.
PY-1: rig-less intervention now; two new wells gated by gas sales agreement.
Cambay: new wells at Palej and sucker rod pumps ordered; new exploration block near Palej in final approval.
demand_pricing: Gas: B-80 gas sold on exchange at about $15-16/MMBTU; Dirok and PY-1 gas pegged at around $10-12/MMBTU; blended realisation $12/MMBTU.
Crude: Kharsang crude sold to Digboi refinery and mainly IOCL; B-80 crude resold to third-party buyers at a loss tied to Brent movements.
HPCL dispute: about INR260 crore invoice plus interest (~INR300 crore) stuck; matter now in conciliation with High Court Chief Justice appointed.
Gas sales route: NRL can act as reseller; management says gas can be sold on exchange within about three days once a credible grid path exists.

qa_highlights.question: When will Dirok's Northeast grid connectivity be complete and when will production ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets December for hot taps by AGCL and the NRL bypass; cited 16-20 weeks lead time for hot taps, which removes the need for an NRL shutdown.

qa_highlights.question: How much loss on the HPCL crude and what would EBITDA be excluding inventory adjustments?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% sold so far with INR4-6 crore loss; further loss estimated at 7-10% of volume, not guidance. CFO declined to quantify EBITDA ex-adjustments, citing inventory, profit petroleum and sale adjustments.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the capex budget increased and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Increase is a contingency for rig availability; capex facility to be drawn as needed. Company is raising debt from investors and banks for B-80 workovers and wells.

qa_highlights.question: Will B-80 workovers fix the structural issue, given past failures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rig intervention can shut off water zones and re-perforate, and cites 2P reserves of 26 MMBOE with 1.5-2 MMBOE produced. Earlier chemical attempts had mixed results.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company provide asset-wise realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO agreed to include offshore and onshore realisations in future presentations; quoted B-80 gas at $16.5/MMBTU and Dirok at $12.5/MMBTU.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gearing and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Gearing 0.04x; total debt is a INR20 crore bank loan.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pass HPCL liability to the buyer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will honour the agreed reversal and resale, preferring a cordial conciliation process with HPCL as a long-term partner.

risks_watch: B-80 water cut rising; outcome of compressor reconfiguration and D1/D2 workovers (October start) and three-well programme dependent on debt financing.
Dirok ramp contingent on DNPL capacity restoration, AGCL hot-tap completion (December target) and NRL bypass; monsoon-related delays already seen.
Kharsang and PY-1 gas monetisation depends on pipeline right-of-way (forest area) and take-or-pay gas agreements.
HPCL crude inventory: further price-linked losses of 7-10% guided; conciliation process unresolved.
Funding: company says B-80 programme depends on raising debt; cash flows not sufficient until late 2027.
Shareholder concern on credibility of production guidance after repeated delays; Tamil Nadu protest on drilling wells raised in the call, with management saying central approvals are in place.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term value and Dirok/Kharsang timelines, but cautious and hedged on B-80 output, funding and HPCL recovery. Several answers were qualified (e.g. "not guidance", "it could be 8,900 or 13,000") and the CFO declined to give EBITDA ex-adjustments.
key_quotes: While certain assets faced short term operational challenges, we made meaningful progress across the portfolio in positioning our key projects for future growth.
We are looking at 500 to 800 barrels per well, and 3 to 5 million scuffs per day from these wells.
So, when I say 11,000, it could be 8,900 or it could be 13,000.
We will not renege on whatever we have agreed with.
So priority-wise, Kharsang is paying for itself, so that's not such a big thing.
Our gearing is very low at this stage. It is 0.04.

adds.what: B-80 two workovers on production (Nov-Dec 2026) and three new wells on production by June 2027, 500-800 bbl per well
Kharsang second phase of nine wells (pending rig award and tubulars, 1-2 months)
Dirok DNPL line restoration to about 2.5 MMSCMD (from 1-1.5 MMSCMD), targeted end-December
Kharsang 24 km pipeline to Bordumsa (14-18 months)
PY-1 two new wells est. 15-20 MMSCFD, gated by take-or-pay gas agreement
Cambay Palej debottlenecking and Balol belt technology, expected 20-30% output increase (5-6% achieved)

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; management held well-level timelines (two B-80 workovers on production Nov-Dec 2026, three wells by June 2027, Dirok DNPL back to 2.5 MMSCMD by end-December), but B-80 funding depends on debt not yet raised, capex was deferred, and Dirok output is capped at 50-70% of well capability by evacuation constraints.
